queue.goal: Formalize the finite matrix game and prove the uniform-equilibrium result by row/column symmetry and zero-sum inequalities.
queue.statement: In a finite two-player zero-sum game whose payoff matrix is circulant and skew-symmetric, the uniform mixed profile is a Nash equilibrium.

queue.goal: Extract the algebraic core from the current Nash candidate into a small axiom-clean Lean module, without invoking a fixed-point existence theorem.
queue.statement: For the finite-game Nash map formed by adding positive deviation gains and renormalizing, a mixed profile is a fixed point if and only if it is a Nash equilibrium.

queue.goal: Define finite correlated equilibrium incentive constraints and prove the point-mass embedding.
queue.statement: The point-mass distribution on any pure Nash equilibrium of a finite game is a correlated equilibrium.

queue.goal: Prove convexity directly from the linear incentive inequalities.
queue.statement: The set of correlated equilibria of a finite game is convex: every convex combination of two correlated equilibria is a correlated equilibrium.

queue.goal: Prove the implication for a supplied mixed Nash equilibrium; do not claim existence of the Nash premise.
queue.statement: The product joint distribution induced by any mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium of a finite game is a correlated equilibrium.

queue.goal: Use well-founded recursion on a finite game tree and prove optimality in every subgame.
queue.statement: Every finite perfect-information extensive-form game with deterministic terminal payoffs has a pure-strategy subgame-perfect equilibrium obtained by backward induction.

queue.goal: Formalize the finite type/action/prior data and prove the equilibrium-preserving normal-form reduction.
queue.statement: A finite Bayesian game with a common prior induces a finite normal-form game on contingent plans, and Bayesian Nash equilibria correspond to Nash equilibria of the induced game.

queue.goal: Prove the finite-time averaging identity directly from the external-regret inequalities.
queue.statement: For a finite repeated game, if every player's external regret after T rounds is at most epsilon times T, then the empirical distribution of joint play is an epsilon-coarse-correlated equilibrium.

queue.goal: Give an executable decision procedure and prove it equivalent to the finite best-response definition.
queue.statement: For a finite game with rational payoffs and a rational mixed profile, whether the profile is a Nash equilibrium is decidable by finitely many exact payoff inequalities.

queue.goal: Pin tie-breaking and utility conventions, then prove truthfulness by cases on the highest competing bid.
queue.statement: In a finite single-item second-price auction with deterministic tie-breaking and quasilinear utilities, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy.
